description: EXAMPLE ONLY -- five invented stations showing the shape vbsd --coords reads, and the three outcomes it distinguishes. The production document is not in this repository: it is a precise point-positioning product covering the live network, and it changes as sites are recomputed. Point --coords at that file; this one exists so the format is documented and the test has something to run against.

EX01._comment: APPLIED. A centimetre-scale correction, which is the normal case and the one that turned out to matter: on real data, shifts of 7-9 mm halved a rover's harmful distance (D146).

EX02._comment: APPLIED. Identical to the registry: an entry agreeing costs nothing and is still worth carrying, because absence and agreement are different facts.

EX03._comment: REFUSED, too far. ~100 km from the registry. The real document contains two entries 160 and 215 km out; a mismatched mountpoint looks exactly the same, and teleporting a base is far worse than a slightly stale coordinate. --coords-max-m bounds it.

EX04._comment: REFUSED on quality. These are computed without a national transformation and sit a median of 0.66 m from the registry -- worse than what they would replace. The file says so; believing it is free.

EX99._comment: NOT IN THE CACHE. The reference document covers stations this network does not serve; they are counted and ignored, never added.
